strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful question: why adversarial training can achieve low robust training error and good clean generalization while retaining a large robust generalization gap.

The proposed combination of shared signal learning and example-specific memorization provides an interpretable mechanism. Studying this mechanism through both representation complexity and training dynamics is a potentially useful contribution.

The MNIST and CIFAR10 capacity experiments, synthetic feature trajectories, and additional loss-landscape measurements provide empirical motivation and several opportunities to connect theory with observed behavior.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under the stated assumptions. Consider two equally likely, well-separated atoms and a linear clean classifier whose boundary lies within the perturbation radius of one atom; this satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3. Once both atoms occur with substantial empirical frequency, vanishing robust training error forces vanishing robust test error, precluding CGRO. The argument needs assumptions controlling sample coverage and ensuring that a substantial population of adversarial errors survives memorization.

The ReLU construction has independent mathematical gaps. Assumption 4.2 separates opposite classes, but does not make same-class training balls disjoint, invalidating the replacement of the union indicator by a sum. Furthermore, continuous ReLU networks cannot uniformly approximate the generally discontinuous function f_S to arbitrarily small error across its jumps, as claimed in Appendix F.1. A valid construction needs explicit transition regions and controls ensuring preservation of classification and robust errors.

Theorem 5.9 does not establish robustness under the paper's definition. Training attacks are restricted to the signal direction, while Definition 3.4 uses the full perturbation ball. Small restricted adversarial loss cannot imply small full-ball robust training error. Indeed, for P=2 under the stated scaling, an ℓ2 attack can replace the patches by αyw*/2 and −3αyw*/5 at cost approximately 0.78α<δ. The tied odd-power network then has negative margin whenever U>0. Thus the claimed learned state can fail robustness even on training examples.

The test-error argument in Theorem E.12 is also unsound as written. A nonzero cubic polynomial of Gaussian variables is not sub-Gaussian, contrary to the concentration argument used for clean generalization. Contributions from different filters share the same Gaussian patches and need not be independent. Moreover, aggregate training memorization V_i=Θ(1) does not imply that every individual noise-weight norm is Θ(1). These gaps affect a principal conclusion rather than merely its presentation.

The additional generalization bound in Theorem B.1 fails a basic sanity check. A nonzero constant-logit classifier has zero input-gradient flatness, but its population logistic loss can exceed its empirical loss with nonvanishing probability because of random label frequencies, even with a smooth input density. The stated bound would incorrectly exclude this sampling fluctuation. Appendix G also retains additive density-estimation terms that are not justified as part of the claimed purely multiplicative flatness bound.

The experiments do not resolve these theoretical concerns. The synthetic setting uses δ=α=10, violating the theorem's δ<α condition and permitting complete signal erasure; robust test failure can therefore arise from information loss. Figure 2(b) and Table 1 report inconsistent CIFAR10 robust test accuracies. PGD step counts, step sizes, restarts, and variability across runs are not adequately specified, limiting reproducibility and confidence in the robustness measurements.

The claimed extension of the exponential lower bound beyond Li et al. (2022) is unclear: Theorem 4.7 is existential over a class already containing linearly separable distributions, and its proof still constructs linearly separable data. Furthermore, a worst-case representation lower bound does not establish that capacity causes the observed failures on the structured distribution or image datasets. The conceptual combination has merit, but the central guarantees require substantial correction before they support acceptance.
